These bounds are then extended to binary and spherical codes via Fourier-analytic methods, where the exponential improvement arises from tighter constraints on the Fourier transform of the code’s characteristic function. The construction of nonsofic groups relies on the interplay between combinatorial expanders and algebraic structures such as the binary Leavitt algebra, demonstrating that certain groups cannot be approximated by sofic ones due to their inherent complexity. Each primitive exhibits a distinct failure mode: sphere packing fails when symmetry is broken, coding theory fails under information-theoretic limits, and group theory fails when algebraic closure is insufficient.
